readout_other: Fura-2 AM ratiometric intracellular Ca2+ imaging
direction_notes: Ultrasound increased intracellular Ca2+ transients in cocultured neurons/astrocytes; response rate rose from 15.4% at 0 V to 76.0% at 66 V, showing a dose-dependent excitatory effect.

exposures.label: pMUT array stimulation of cocultured cortical neurons and astrocytes

timing.protocol_description: Pulses of 100 cycles of sinusoidal ultrasound were applied at a pulse repetition frequency of 2 kHz. For calcium-imaging experiments, cells were monitored for 120 s baseline, then the transducer was turned on continuously for 180 s (120-300 s), followed by 300 s of post-stimulation observation. Intensity was varied via input voltage (0-66 V) at a fixed distance (1 mm) and frequency; a separate localization test varied horizontal distance from the active transducer channel.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The peak intensity of $1 . 1 2 2 \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ that was measured at 430 kHz with an input voltage of 66 V was identical to the impedance result (Fig. 5b).
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.isppa_w_cm2: The acoustic intensity was found to range from 0.025 to $1 . 1 2 2 \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ when the input voltage of pMUTs was varied from 11 to 66 V (Fig. 5c).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: To actuate the pMUTs, we used a function generator (33500B; Agilent, USA) to apply 100 cycles of sinusoidal sound waves with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 2 kHz, which is the effective value for stimulating neurons and astrocytes<sup>14</sup>.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Then, we monitored $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ transients for 120 s as a control experiment and turned on the ultrasound transducer for 180 s (from 120 s to 300 s), followed by observing $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ transients for 300 s after the transducer was turned off.
